name: WordPress
support: Open-source project supported by a worldwide developer community and commercial hosting providers.
technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL or MariaDB. Client: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
capabilities: Custom themes, plugins, block editor, media management, REST API, and SEO extensions.
limitations: Requires regular updates. Third-party plugins may introduce security risks, compatibility problems, and performance issues.

name: Drupal
support: Open-source CMS maintained by the Drupal community and supported by organizations including the Drupal Association.
technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, or SQLite. Client: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
capabilities: Custom content types, user permissions, multilingual support, content workflows, modules, and API-based publishing.
limitations: Has a steeper learning curve. Complex customization and upgrades may require experienced developers and additional maintenance.

name: Joomla
support: Open-source CMS supported by the Joomla community and Open Source Matters.
technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL. Client: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
capabilities: Templates, extensions, multilingual websites, user access controls, menus, and content management.
limitations: Extension compatibility and updates require attention. Advanced customizations can require technical knowledge.

name: Ghost
support: Open-source publishing platform developed by Ghost Foundation, with commercial Ghost(Pro) hosting available.
technology: Server: Node.js. Database: MySQL for production installations. Client: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
capabilities: Blog publishing, newsletters, memberships, paid subscriptions, custom themes, and content APIs.
limitations: Mainly focused on publishing and newsletters. More complex website features may require custom development or third-party integrations.

name: TYPO3
support: Open-source enterprise CMS supported by the TYPO3 Association, developer community, and professional agencies.
technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, or SQLite. Client: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
capabilities: Multilingual content, enterprise permissions, multisite management, custom extensions, content workflows, and integrations.
limitations: Requires technical expertise for installation and customization. Development and maintenance can be more complex for small websites.
